deep_audit_observations.finding: This is not a named theoretical presentation, so it is outside the normal named-theory closeout surface. The reachable ballot-routed Proposition 1 theorem establishes the per-district rounded STV/PAV outcome. The checked vote-share selector theorem separately proves only a per-query rounded-pair refinement and a five-operation arithmetic certificate. Neither result proves the paper's empirical whole-map implementation, its data pipeline, or a runtime bound for the stated optimization workload.
deep_audit_observations.scope_note: Do not award named-result credit for this prose. A future deep-paper review of the computational claim must state the map-search algorithm, input representation, number and construction of district queries, cost model, and the exact relationship between the per-query selector and the implementation. It must then prove any claimed aggregate complexity or validate it as an empirical measurement. The existing rounded outcome theorem and per-query selector certificate may be reused only after that interface is specified.
deep_audit_observations.source_claim: The unnumbered prose around Proposition 1 says that party seat shares can be calculated up to rounding from vote shares without voter rankings, and says the resulting shortcut is used while optimizing about 10^12 maps for one state.

defects.acceptance_condition: Lean derives the quota-fit and rounded-seat bounds for every natural V satisfying the source's V at least M(M+1) hypothesis, including nondivisible V.
defects.repair_obligation: Prove the quota capacity and party lower-bound arithmetic for Q = floor(V/(M+1)) + 1 without assuming divisibility of V by M+1.
defects.resolution_evidence: The theorem paper_stv_quota_floors_fit and the generated filled-seat STV support theorem use the exact floor Droop quota and quantify over arbitrary natural turnout under the source lower bound; no divisibility premise appears.
defects.source_claim: Proposition 1 covers every integer electorate size V at least M(M+1), but its appendix proof temporarily assumes V is divisible by M+1 and says without derivation that the same arguments extend.
defects.status_impact_rationale: This is a minor omitted arithmetic case in the source proof, not a changed theorem. Lean proves the general floor-Droop-quota arithmetic over the full stated integer domain, so this issue does not leave a partial-formalization boundary.

defects.acceptance_condition: A source-facing Proposition 1 theorem starts from the source ballot/candidate/transfer-rule model and derives the actual terminal STV run and global-to-party refinement internally for every admitted transfer rule. It may not accept rawRun, refinement, projected party paths, party tally conservation, or party winner counts as theorem-facing premises. A checked fractional-run specialization remains support rather than source-wide credit.
defects.repair_obligation: Define the source-admitted class of surplus-preserving STV transfer rules operationally on complete ranked ballots, then derive a terminal global execution and its complete two-party refinement from the source candidate sets, solid-coalition rankings, quota rule, and transfer semantics. In particular derive the party candidate partition, projected initial tallies, pre-exhaustion mass conservation, transition serialization, and winner-update coherence instead of receiving them in a raw-run record.
defects.resolution_evidence: BallotRoutedSTV.lean defines the source rule on reachable voter-weight states: a quota election removes exactly one quota from the elected candidate's actual support, leaves off-support ballots unchanged, and never increases a supporting ballot's retained weight; elimination leaves ballot weights unchanged while routing changes through the active set, and nonnegative state weights are preserved. FractionalBallotRoutedBridge.lean proves the fractional runner satisfies those laws. BallotRoutedSTVExecution.lean constructs a finite terminal execution without a caller-supplied trace. BallotRoutedSTVPartyInvariant.lean derives the party projections and conservation laws from these transitions. BallotRoutedSTVProposition1.lean derives both party lower bounds from the actual common prefix and terminal state. PaperInterface.paper_proposition1_all_ballot_routed_surplus_transfer_outcomes_and_selected_pav quantifies over every terminal execution and accepts no rawRun, refinement, local path, conservation equality, or terminal seat count as an input. The old SourceSurplusPreservingPartyTransferRule interface is separately proved noninhabited on arbitrary malformed states and is quarantined as legacy support only.
defects.source_claim: The rounded STV conclusion of Proposition 1 is independent of the surplus-preserving transfer rule, including transfer rules other than the fractional implementation used in simulations.
defects.source_locator: cited publication:403-410; cited publication:492-498; cited publication:2497-2553
defects.status_impact_rationale: The former generic theorem was not an admissible source endpoint: its raw-run refinement contained the central global-to-party proof bridge. The replacement quantifies only over a reachable ballot-routed transfer policy and derives party mass accounting, the common cutoff, terminal outcomes, and a nonvacuous terminal execution from actual ballot transitions. The historical defect is therefore repaired rather than reclassified as a source assumption.
